crates.name: psx-rt
crates.purpose: Bare-metal runtime: `_start`, BIOS calls, panic, heap, VBlank IRQ counter, corrected i64 builtins, scratchpad regions and scratchpad stacks.

crates.name: psx-io
crates.purpose: Volatile MMIO primitives for target code, plus the CD-ROM command surface.

crates.name: psx-gpu
crates.purpose: High-level GPU API: init, primitives, framebuffers, display-window shifting.

crates.name: psx-vram
crates.purpose: Typed VRAM layout primitives: color, rect, tpage, CLUT, upload helpers.

crates.name: psx-spu
crates.purpose: High-level SPU API: typed voices, volume, pitch, ADSR, ADPCM upload, key-on/off, loop chaining, noise.

crates.name: psx-sfx
crates.purpose: SPU effects: sample banks, the length-based one-shot cutoff, a host-testable voice mixer (lanes, priorities, handles, virtual loops), spatial gains and master volumes.

crates.name: psx-seq
crates.purpose: Sequenced music on the SPU: a script interpreter (sequence, channel, layer), software envelopes, vibrato and portamento, and a note allocator over `psx-sfx`'s hardware seam.

crates.name: psx-settings
crates.purpose: Versioned game preferences with optional memory-card persistence.

crates.name: psx-segments
crates.purpose: Bounded segment selection and launch requests using game-owned state and controls.

crates.name: psx-display
crates.purpose: Picture options: the BRIGHTNESS stepper (`DEFAULT`, `DARKER n`, `BRIGHTER n`) with its one-packet GPU overlay, and the SCREEN X/Y stepper, each with row text and a save byte. Host-tested, no heap ([adoption guide](https://github.com/EBonura/PSoXide/tree/main/sdk/docs/DISPLAY-OPTIONS.md)).

crates.name: psx-loading
crates.purpose: An animated LOADING indicator for blocking loads: a label with stepping dots or a dot spinner and a breathing ink, drawn as plain GP0 rectangles from any `BitmapFont` (no VRAM, no atlas, no heap). Polled from a load loop, redraws only when the picture changes. Host-tested ([adoption guide](https://github.com/EBonura/PSoXide/tree/main/sdk/docs/LOADING-INDICATOR.md)).

crates.name: psx-gte
crates.purpose: GTE (COP2) wrappers. MIPS emits inline-asm coprocessor ops; host routes through `psx-gte-core`.

crates.name: psx-gte-core
crates.purpose: Pure-Rust GTE state machine and fixed-point math. Shared by `psx-gte` and the emulator; bit-exact against a real-console conformance corpus.

crates.name: psx-math
crates.purpose: Fixed-point math: Q0.12 angles + sin/cos/atan2, int32 helpers, decimal text formatting.

crates.name: psx-pad
crates.purpose: SIO0 controller polling: digital + DualShock analog, `PadTracker` edges/repeat, diagnostic pacing. Feature `irq-engine`: the interrupt-driven engine that polls both ports from VBlank and IRQ7 without waiting ([PAD-IRQ-ENGINE](https://github.com/EBonura/PSoXide/tree/main/sdk/docs/PAD-IRQ-ENGINE.md)).

crates.name: psx-tick
crates.purpose: Fixed-timestep game clock: per-game tick rate and catch-up policy, a render phase for interpolation, and consistency counters. Callers pass the VBlank count, so every rule is host-testable.

crates.name: psx-font
crates.purpose: Bitmap-font atlas: 1bpp source → 4bpp CLUT VRAM texture, GP0 textured-rect draw path.

crates.name: psx-fx
crates.purpose: Arcade-style visual effects: particle pools, screen shake, deterministic RNG.

crates.name: psx-asset
crates.purpose: Runtime parsers for cooked-asset blobs. Consumes `psxed-format` layouts produced by the editor.

crates.name: psx-cache
crates.purpose: Generic no_std slot cache: keyed residency pool with LRU eviction and pinning.

crates.name: psx-mc
crates.purpose: Memory-card driver: SIO0 transport, on-card filesystem format interoperable with the console's card manager, optional LZSS compression.

crates.name: psx-osk
crates.purpose: On-screen keyboard for pad-driven text entry: QWERTY/symbols pages, shift, PS4-style boxed keys.

crates.name: psx-pack
crates.purpose: Guest-side WORLD.PAK parsing + in-place HLZC/LZ4 decompression (reader half of `psx-iso`).

crates.name: psx-cdstream
crates.purpose: Interrupt-driven CD streaming: a queue of read requests drained one sector per drive interrupt, seek-first, abortable at the next sector, contiguous requests chained without a seek, and a drive arbiter for CD-DA. The state machine is host-tested against a scripted drive.

crates.name: psx-residency
crates.purpose: Residency policy for streamed data: contiguous page pools with generation handles, priority classes, pinning, distance-then-LRU eviction, retry backoff, and a fixed-slot policy. It decides what to load and what to evict and never touches the drive; reads go out through a trait. Host-tested, no heap.

crates.name: psx-residency-sim
crates.purpose: Host-only route simulator for `psx-residency`: replays a route through a region graph against the real policy and a drive model built from the silicon seek and read measurements, and reports deadline slack and misses.

crates.name: psx-telemetry
crates.purpose: Shared guest/host telemetry id tables for the emulator profiling hooks.

crates.name: psx-fmv
crates.purpose: FMV playback building blocks: STR sector demux, BS v2 bitstream to MDEC run-length decode, MDEC upload/decode via DMA0/DMA1 (guest only), ISO9660 root-file lookup.

examples.name: hello-tri
examples.shows: A single GPU triangle.

examples.name: hello-tex
examples.shows: Textured primitives + CLUT upload.

examples.name: hello-ot
examples.shows: Ordering-table depth sorting.

examples.name: hello-input
examples.shows: Controller polling via `psx-pad`.

examples.name: sfxbench
examples.shows: Cycles the `psx-sfx` bookkeeping costs: placement gains, the mixer's level update, an idle tick and a stealing `play`.

examples.name: hello-seq
examples.shows: Plays a song cooked by `psx-seq-cook` from the player's own cartridge through `psx-seq` and reports what the sequencer costs.

examples.name: pollbench
examples.shows: Cycles one synchronous controller poll costs: port 1, an empty port 2, both.

examples.name: pad-engine-check
examples.shows: The interrupt-driven pad engine against the synchronous driver: CPU left to the game, snapshot, lease.

examples.name: hello-gte
examples.shows: GTE-accelerated transforms.

examples.name: hello-audio
examples.shows: SPU voice playback.

examples.name: hello-cdda
examples.shows: CD-DA audio tracks.

examples.name: hello-xa
examples.shows: XA-ADPCM music: four generated songs interleaved in one file, played through `psx_io::cd::xa` with a pad-driven switch (`make hello-xa-disc`).

examples.name: hello-xa-resume
examples.shows: An XA song surviving a data read: suspends it, reads sectors through the polled reader, resumes, and checks the head, the song clock, the drive command log and the audio (`make hello-xa-resume-gate`).

examples.name: hello-spstack
examples.shows: A call tree run on a scratchpad stack under VBlank IRQs, checked against the RAM stack; `stack-guard` (`tools/psoxide-hazard`) proves it fits.

examples.name: hello-gteirq
examples.shows: RTPS run under VBlank IRQs, checking that psx-rt's handler never runs a GTE command twice. The emulator models this since its commit c7e3ea8; a console run remains the reference.

examples.name: hello-present
examples.shows: psx-rt's queued display flip, held until the frame's closing GP0(1Fh) sets GPUSTAT bit 24 (`arm_draw_done`, `end_with_draw_done`, `signal_draw_done`).

examples.name: hello-diag
examples.shows: The console stop-panel (`psx-rt` feature `console-diag`) shown on purpose: a stall, a fault, a panic, a failed CD read, an oversized GPU list node or a jump to nowhere (`wild`), chosen by `HELLO_DIAG_MODE`. See [CONSOLE-STOP-PANEL](https://github.com/EBonura/PSoXide/tree/main/sdk/docs/CONSOLE-STOP-PANEL.md).

examples.name: hello-fault
examples.shows: Panics on purpose (an out-of-range index) so `tools/abort_gate.sh` can prove a `panic=immediate-abort` guest records the `break` in `__psx_rt_fault_*` and that `psoxide-size faults` names `main`; the shared panic policy lives in `tools/psoxide-size`.

examples.name: hello-present-queue
examples.shows: psx-rt's VBlank-kicked present queue (`present-queue` feature): whole frames published as one chain each, preamble and HUD recorded with `psx_io::gpu::start_recording_raw`, kicked and flipped by the VBlank handler.

examples.name: hello-fmv
examples.shows: FMV console test: streams a 2x STR with XA audio, decodes it with `psx-fmv`, and shows sector counts (LOST/BAD) over the video.

examples.name: hello-memcard
examples.shows: Non-destructive memory-card diagnostic: reads and hashes all 1024 frames, then (L1+R1+Cross) writes and verifies one test save.

examples.name: hello-memprobe
examples.shows: Checks psx-rt's `memcpy`/`memset`/`memcmp` against reference loops for every size and alignment; prints `MEMPROBE PASS` or `FAIL`.

examples.name: hello-asmprobe
examples.shows: Differential test and cycle benchmark for the hand-scheduled kernels (`psx-gpu` and `psx-math` `asm-kernels`): bit-identical against the portable definition on random and edge inputs, then timed; prints `ASMPROBE PASS` or `FAIL` and `BENCH` lines.

examples.name: hello-pack
examples.shows: `psx_pack::cd` smoke test: streams raw and compressed WORLD.PAK chunks off the disc and checks them.

examples.name: hello-cdstream
examples.shows: `psx-cdstream` on a disc: single, chained, prioritised, aborted-and-resumed and sustained reads of a known file checked byte for byte, an audio lease taken mid-read, and the foreground cost of a long read (`make hello-cdstream-disc`, `make hello-cdstream-gate`).

examples.name: hello-cdpause
examples.shows: The console's two-response Pause against `SectorReader::stop_proved`: the second response 1.2 to 3.9 million clocks after the first, a Pause refused during a seek and sent again (`make hello-cdpause-disc`, `make hello-cdpause-gate`; needs an emulator with the silicon Pause model).

examples.name: hello-wide
examples.shows: Every `psx_math::Wide` / `WideU` / `Mask64` operation against a reference built from 32-bit arithmetic only, on the target; prints `WIDE PASS` or `FAIL`. Its link map must pass the symbol gate (`make hello-wide-gate`).

examples.name: hello-wide-div
examples.shows: Every `psx_math::wide_div` operation (division of a `Wide` / `WideU`, 128-bit product, ratio compare) against a bit-by-bit 32-bit reference, on the target; prints `WIDEDIV PASS` or `FAIL` and the cycles per call of each. Its link map must pass the symbol gate (`make hello-wide-gate`).

examples.name: hello-i64probe
examples.shows: Runs software 64-bit multiply/divide/modulo on the target and checks the results; covers psx-rt's `__divdi3`/`__moddi3` overrides.

examples.name: hello-icache
examples.shows: Rewrites a function in cached RAM and checks that `psx_rt::cache::flush_instruction_cache` makes the CPU run the new code; prints `ICACHE PASS`, `INCONCLUSIVE` (nothing was stale) or `FAIL`.

examples.name: hello-overlay
examples.shows: Same-compilation Rust cold entry and resident service, caller-owned arena, scoped static-call binding and unload/re-admit generation checks. Uses its own checked packaging recipe; see [the example](https://github.com/EBonura/PSoXide/tree/main/sdk/examples/hello-overlay/README.md).

examples.name: cdda-read-contention
examples.shows: CD-ROM conformance probe: issues a data read while CD-DA is playing and records which IRQ the drive raises.
